headline: Decimals are fractions in disguise—expressing parts using powers of ten
universal_truth: Different representations of the same thing reveal different insights
fun_facts: The decimal point was invented around 1593 by mathematician Christopher Clavius
0.999... (repeating forever) equals exactly 1—mathematically proven, though counterintuitive
Money uses decimals because our currency system is based on powers of ten
discussion_questions: Why do we use decimals for money but fractions for recipes?
When are decimals easier to work with than fractions?
Can every fraction become a decimal?

hook.script: One half. Point five. Zero point five zero zero. These all mean the same thing—just written differently. Decimals are fractions that use powers of ten, making calculation easier and comparison instant.

cliff.script: If fractions already work, why invent decimals? What advantage do decimal representations have that made them worth creating?
cliff.prompt: Why did decimals become so popular?

options.text: Decimals are easier to compare, calculate with, and line up for addition
options.response: Yes. Comparing 0.75 to 0.8 is instant. Comparing 3/4 to 4/5 requires thought. Decimals enable faster math.

options.text: Decimals are more accurate than fractions
options.response: Actually, fractions can be more precise—1/3 is exact, while 0.333... goes on forever...

fact1.title: Position Is Power
fact1.script: In decimals, position determines value. The first place after the dot is tenths, then hundredths, then thousandths. Each step right divides by ten. This 'place value' system makes arithmetic systematic.

fact2.title: Repeating Mysteries
fact2.script: Some fractions become repeating decimals: 1/3 = 0.333... forever. Stranger still: 0.999... repeating infinitely equals exactly 1. Not approximately—exactly. The proof is surprising but airtight.

fact3.title: Money System
fact3.script: Currency uses decimals—$4.99, £12.50—because our number system is base ten. It's why we have 100 cents in a dollar, 100 pence in a pound. Decimals and money were designed together.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Different representations reveal different insights. Fractions and decimals express the same values but serve different purposes. The best tool depends on the task. Flexibility beats rigidity.

outro.script: That's Day 102. Tomorrow, we'll explore 'out of a hundred'—percentages. Until then, notice where you see decimals and consider what fractions they represent.

growTrack.title: Decimal Translation - See the Fraction
growTrack.learning_objective: Connect decimals to their fraction equivalents
growTrack.activity: When you see a decimal today—a price, a measurement, a percentage—translate it to a fraction. $0.50 = 1/2. 0.25 = 1/4. Practice seeing both representations to strengthen your number sense.
